description: Updated   added a number of pages at the start  (from page 2) that describes the entire system and whats missing apologies for not giving this overview of  what would happen given those missing parts and the purpose of demo0.01 which substitute those parts to see whether the break down of the 10 miliscond to (longer period) with each handwritten sim, does stack chems as mentioned; and thus imply correct behavior some of the documents mentioning demo 0.01 and its motivation wasnt included (mentioned in the catpilot) therefore might cause confusion  (ontop of also not really mentioning what would each of the missing part cause,) much apologies   part 1 and part 2 updated of the emulated cat goes along with these documents: pilot:  https://zenodo.org/records/14737043 beacons: https://zenodo.org/records/14737060 bevcyc: https://zenodo.org/records/14737076

methods.name: Independent vision-processing modules (Scanning Trio, Track Trio)
methods.description: Proposes organ-like modules (modScan/modLoc/modNav for maps, points, routes; modWatch/modLook/modTude for shading, attention, tests) that process vision input and publish triggers.
methods.evidence: This part deals with the : LABELING & TAGGING of objects (ScanTrio ; TrackTrio)

methods.name: Chempool emulation of accumulated chemicals/hormones
methods.description: Uses chempool nodes attached to modules to tally stacked chemical notations (e.g. STRESS^, #ERROR) that time and combine trigger initiation.
methods.evidence: Chempools are a depiction / special node to tally Accumulated affectors / chemicals / hormones That emulate how a organ depend on this triggers / combo

methods.name: CYC drivers decomposed into |n| slots by a CYC modulator
methods.description: Epigenetic-emulation CYC drivers (e.g. WAKE-HAPPY-WAKE) are split into six-slot blocks force-filled from priority tables set by the CYC modulator, then resolved.
methods.evidence: Dividing each CYC block onto | n n n n n n | six smaller blocks insisting on updates / force filling from the priority tables (decided by CYC-modulator); and then resolving each block

methods.name: modStream trigger grading into themes, latches and simulations
methods.description: Triggers from the vision trios (and CYCs) are graded by modStream into themes and latches (simulations), which modLatch resolves into updates.
methods.evidence: Taking CYCs and Triggers (from Trios) onto THEMES & LATCHES (sims)

methods.name: Planned DEMO 0.01 with hardcoded CYCs and simulations
methods.description: Proposes a demo that handwrites 11 CYCs and a simple map simulation, 'cheats' the PRM step, and shows chem accumulation and trigger selection without learning.
methods.evidence: Then cheat the PRM step; simply show a Tree; on what was decided

key_findings: The authors state the document's purpose is only to justify the proposed flow, which is a posit testable only once its components exist.
They list missing components, including sim, CYC and chem tables, the CYC modulator (a process reward model), a trigger table and a sim resolver.
The authors argue a process reward model is critical: without it, it would be impossible to check which route or CYC completion was better.
The authors flag as untested whether the proposed decreasing-slot protocol for breaking down CYCs is valid or runs smoothly.
key_findings_evidence: The purpose of the paper is actually only to justify the Flow On which itself is, :/ actually just a posit; that would only be test-able Given that these components already exist;
Currently missing parts are: 1. Sim table 2. Cyc table 3. Chem table 4. Cyc modulator
But the PRM is critical / process reward model (alphago like break-down-of-the-steps?) On which without such knowledge or implementation; it would be impossible To check which route was done better

summary_provenance.method: Evidence-grounded extraction from full_text.md: every method and finding carries a verbatim quote from the paper text, mechanically verified to occur in full_text.md (whitespace/ligature-normalized) before merge.
summary_provenance.notes: Informal, slide/notes-style conceptual design document for a cat-hippocampus agent; nothing has been implemented or tested in the text, and the authors repeatedly flag uncertainty ('We are not quite sure yet!'). Extraction of several pages is fragmentary (columns split). Bibliography domain is 'Genetics & Biomedical', which fits the content poorly (it is an agent-architecture proposal), though the text makes no genetics claims beyond a 'speculative Epigenetic Basis' framing.
